title: Agent Playbook Operator Manifest (sketch)
content:
Goal:
This is a personal scratchpad for an "Agent Playbook Operator" manifest format. The idea: provide teams a compact, machine-friendly, and human-editable manifest for operator-run agent playbooks (task orchestration + fallback policies + telemetry hooks). Deliverable should cover: config shape, runtime API surface, validation rules, and a minimal illustrative YAML+HTTP examples for the operator server.

Context / why: 
- We want a standard on top of runtime orchestration that lets non-infra teams declare agent workflows (tool sequences, gating, SLOs, fallback variants) and hand them to Redwood Dedicated/Private operator to run with observability and safe guardrails.
- This lives at the intersection of runtime routing (serving), policy (safety/backoff), and product (reusable prompts/tool chains).

Design goals (tradeoffs):
- Compact: single-playbook file should be editable in a PR.
- Composable: allow referencing shared components (tools, prompts).
- Safe by default: deny-globally for tool actions unless whitelisted by tenant policy.
- Observable: telemetry hooks and sample sets included in manifest for quality checks.
- Versioned and immutable: operator stores manifest version, supports canary rollouts.

Key concepts (terms we use below):
- Playbook: top-level manifest for one agent workflow.
- Step: atomic unit; calls model or tool; has inputs/outputs and success/failure transitions.
- Variant: alternate model/tool config used for fallback or cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Trigger: event or API route that activates a playbook.
- Hook: telemetry/validation callouts (pre/post).

Schema sketch (flattened fields for readability):
- apiVersion: v1alpha.playbook
- kind: AgentPlaybook
- metadata: name, namespace, labels, annotations, owner
- spec: 
  - description: short freeform
  - triggers: list of { type: http | schedule | event, route: string, method: GET/POST (for http), schedule: cron }
  - entry: step-id that is starting node
  - steps: ordered map stepId -> {
      type: model | tool | condition | parallel | merge,
      impl: for model -> { model: name, version: v, variant: optional },
      impl: for tool -> { tool: name, action: id, args: mapping },
      timeout_ms: integer,
      retries: { max: int, backoff_ms: int },
      transitions: { on_success: stepId | end, on_failure: stepId | fallback | end },
      outputs: list of named outputs (for wiring)
    }
  - variants: map of variantId -> { cpu/quant/latency_hint, cost_estimate, model_alias }
  - policy: { allowed_tools: list, blocked_tokens: list, max_user_context_tokens: int }
  - telemetry: { sample_set: id, metrics: [latency, cost, accuracy_probe], hooks: { pre: url, post: url } }
  - rollout: { strategy: immediate | canary, canary: { percent: int, duration: seconds } }
  - constraints: { max_concurrent_runs: int, per_tenant_qps: int }

Example (illustrative YAML-like snippet):

apiVersion: v1alpha.playbook
kind: AgentPlaybook
metadata:
  name: product-summary-assistant
  owner: teams/growth
spec:
  description: "Summarize product notes into release-ready copy, call search tool if unclear"
  triggers:
    - type: http
      route: /playbooks/product-summary
      method: POST
  entry: step-1
  steps:
    step-1:
      type: model
      impl:
        model: redwood-internal/llama-3-small
      timeout_ms: 5000
      transitions:
        on_success: step-2
        on_failure: fallback-variant-1
    step-2:
      type: condition
      impl:
        expression: "known_entities_present(outputs.step-1)"
      transitions:
        on_success: step-3
        on_failure: step-lookup
    step-lookup:
      type: tool
      impl:
        tool: elastic-search
        action: query
        args: { q: "{{outputs.step-1.summary_query}}", top_k: 3 }
      transitions: { on_success: step-3, on_failure: end }
    step-3:
      type: model
      impl: { model: open/llama-3-medium, variant: cheap-quant }
      transitions: { on_success: end, on_failure: end }
  variants:
    cheap-quant: { latency_hint: low, cost_estimate: 0.02 }
  policy:
    allowed_tools: [elastic-search, notifier]
  telemetry:
    sample_set: release-summary-v1
    metrics: [latency, tokens, error_rate]
    hooks: { pre: https://ops-hooks/redwood/playbook/pre, post: https://ops-hooks/redwood/playbook/post }
  rollout: { strategy: canary, canary: { percent: 10, duration: 3600 } }

Operator HTTP API (runtime):
- POST /v1/playbooks: register manifest (body = YAML/JSON) -> 201 + { id }
- GET /v1/playbooks/{id}: fetch manifest + versions
- POST /v1/playbooks/{id}: create new version (operator validates, dry-run)
- POST /v1/playbooks/{id}/runs: start a run (payload = trigger context), returns run_id + immediate status
- GET /v1/runs/{run_id}: stream events (step-start, step-end, metrics)
- POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/abort: abort in-flight run

Runtime contract / validation rules (sketch):
- Steps must form a DAG (no cycles except explicit loop nodes)
- Tool actions must be in allowed_tools list or tenant-global allowlist
- Model variant fallback chain must be acyclic and resolve to existing variant ids
- Max manifest size (bytes) and max steps enforced to prevent runaway complexity
- All hooks must be HTTPS with cert validation; operator may replace host with internal proxied hook for auditing

Telemetry & safety hooks:
- pre-hook: called with sanitized context (PII redaction) before run starts, used for gating and quick-metrics
- post-hook: receives run outcome, step-level metrics (latency, tokens, errors), and an anonymized trace for QA
- periodic sample: operator stores sampled transcripts, configurable by spec.sample_set

Edge cases / open questions (TODO):
- Authorization model: manifest-level scoping vs tenant-level allowlist. Who can register playbooks? RBAC mapping to console teams?
- Cost accounting: if a playbook uses multiple variants/tools across tenants, how to allocate cost and quota? (should be per-run breakdown)
- Debugging UX: need a "dry-run" simulation mode that returns estimated token costs / trace without billing. (for devs)
- Local development: small dev operator binary to run manifests locally and record trace format compatible with operator (proto+JSON)
- Model safety: where to plug content-moderation? step-level policy vs global prefilter?

Developer UX notes (personal):
- Keep the manifest compact; avoid repeating long prompt bodies in the file. Use references to shared prompts by name + version. Allow prompt overrides via run-time inputs.
- Recommend a "recipe" doc in repo showing common patterns: search->summarize->notify; or multi-tool coordination.

Implementation sketch for operator side (runtime):
1) Ingest manifest, validate, store as immutable version.
2) Translate steps into an execution graph with resource hints (gpu/cpu).
3) Schedule step tasks on serving runtime via existing /v1/execute endpoints, passing tenant context + telemetry id.
4) Enforce tool whitelist at call-time via proxy.
5) Emit structured events to tracing backend and call post-hook.
6) Support canary by routing X% of requests to new version using existing routing layer.

Minimal JSON schema (just key field types) to include in operator validation library:
- apiVersion: string
- kind: string
- metadata.name: string
- spec.triggers: array
- spec.entry: string
- spec.steps: object{ string -> object }
(Will formalize as JSON Schema later)

Next steps (my action items):
- Share with Avery & Diego for quick sanity check (ask: do we need explicit 'compensation' step semantics?)
- Draft a lightweight JSON Schema and validation unit tests (RDW-2387)
- Prototype a small local runner lib (Python) that accepts manifest + test harness and outputs step traces
- Create a Confluence page describing RBAC and allowed_tools policy model

Notes on related artifacts:
- Related GH PR: playbooks/pull/42 (linked above) has early protos for step events
- Slack thread: #prod-playbooks (search: "playbook operator sketch")

Random brain-dump ideas (may be useful later):
- Allow 'simulated' step types useful for load/latency testing (returns canned outputs)
- Add a "cost window" selector so teams can request cheaper variants during high load windows automatically
- Allow "explain" flag to expand abbreviated telemetry into richer debugging output for dev runs only

-- end of scratchpad --

Unresolved: I intentionally left the exact JSON Schema and example prompt references out; will follow up with a more formal draft that includes schema + sample test harness.
